text:
cory_customer: Hi team — we're seeing INVALID_JSON errors from the API when returning JSON mode for some user inputs. Repro attached, customer hit this in production and it breaks downstream parsers.

jess_support: Thanks Cory. Can you paste the minimal prompt + params you used? Also, any request_id or trace id from the logs?

cory_customer: repro steps:
1) curl POST to /v1/generate with `mode: \"json\"`, `stream: true`
2) prompt contains ASCII control char U+000B (vertical tab) and a Windows-style CRLF mix
3) client-side JSON.parse throws: `SyntaxError: Unexpected token \u000b in JSON at position 198`

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXX' -d '{"model":"open-xyz","mode":"json","input":"Line1\r\nLine2\u000bLine3"}'

request_id: req_ck7b2gq1 trace: t-9a4f

devon_sre: I see an error in the proxy logs: `chunked output terminated mid-string` and downstream parser sees `...\"field\": \"Line1\r\nLine2\u000` (truncated). Looks like streaming boundaries split an escape sequence.

alim_eng: This smells like our chunker/escape stitching logic in json mode. If a backslash-u escape or control char is split across SSE frames we might not be reassembling before unescaping. Reproducer is great, I'll try local.

jess_support: Customer reports this started after last runtime deploy (yesterday ~21:10 UTC). Could be related to the new streaming buffer change.

devon_sre: Also noticed a latency spike for those requests: p95 went from 120ms to 500ms for that route during the incident window. Possibly retries from client causing extra load.

ryan_billing: Heads up — the customer is seeing unexpectedly high token usage because they re-request when parse fails. They want a credit if it's on our side. Keeping billing in loop.

alim_eng: Quick workaround for customers: set `stream:false` or `json_mode: \"lenient\"` (if they can accept non-strict output) while we triage. For prod fix I'll add extra buffering to ensure we don't break escape sequences across chunks.

devon_sre: Can you also attach the raw SSE payload from the proxy logs? I want to confirm where the split happens.

cory_customer: Pasting raw sse snippet we captured:

```
event: token
data: {"id":"tok_1","text":"...\\u000bLine3"}

event: token
data: {"id":"tok_2","text":"...\\u000bLine4"}

event: done

```

jess_support: Hmm the raw shows double-escaped sequences coming through, then the client unescapes and gets a literal control char, and then the stream ends mid-escape.

alim_eng: Reproduced locally. Repro failure mode: when the escape sequence `\\u000b` is split so the `u000b` lands in the next frame, our unescape pass treats the fragment as literal and we emit a raw control char, which later truncation makes invalid JSON. Fix plan: rework SSE chunk stitching to operate on the encoded stream level and only unescape after full JSON object reassembly. Also add a regression test with embedded control chars + CRLF mixes.

devon_sre: Deployment plan? Can we hotfix proxy to buffer up to 4KB per stream to avoid splits, and ship the proper fix in next runtime patch?

alim_eng: Yes — hotfix buffer now, full fix next day. Will push a staged rollout and monitor.

jess_support: Noted. I'll reply to the customer with the workaround and ETA for hotfix. Apologize and offer provisional credit per billing.

ryan_billing: I'll earmark a one-time credit pending root cause. Please include impacted request_ids and time window.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1047 — streaming-json-escape-split. Priority P2.

cory_customer: Thanks all — workaround applied, I'll confirm if parsing is stable. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

devon_sre: Adding metrics alert: if parse errors for json_mode > 5% for 5m, escalate to oncall automatically.

alim_eng: Pushed hotfix to canary, no regressions so far and stitch failure rate dropped in local. Will schedule full rollout in 30m.

jess_support: TY! keep me posted and I'll update the customer thread with the canary results.
